rows.title: Ask 'What are you importing?' before a notification is created
rows.detail: Starting a new notification from the all-types dashboard in the INS front door asks the Design Release 2.1 notification type question first, before any draft exists. Live animals carries on to the animals frontend's existing start, which creates the GBN-AG draft and lands on origin; Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products carry on to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend. Germinal products is left off the list because no real service takes it. Abandoning the question leaves no empty draft behind. The origin page's Back link then follows where the user came from: the type question, the live-animals category dashboard, or the overview.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a new notification from the all-types dashboard shows the question 'What are you importing?' instead of going straight to an origin page, and no draft notification is created at that point: the dashboard's notification list gains no new entry while the question is open or after the user leaves it with Back (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11112-11114; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1; trace:e2e T01 call@286; conflicts:c-007)

The notification type page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'What are you importing?' as the radios' fieldset legend (h1), with the caption 'About the consignment' inside the heading (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:7,39; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)

The question offers radios in this order, with no hint text on the group or any option and none pre-selected: Live animals; Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products. Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) is not offered (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:125-138; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Live animals and pressing Continue creates a new live-animals draft and lands on its 'Origin of the import' page, which shows the Draft tag and a new GBN-AG reference (prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:65; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-007)

Choosing Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) or Wood products and pressing Continue lands on the start of the high-risk plants journey in the plants service, and no live-animals notification is created (conflicts:c-007)

Pressing Continue with nothing chosen re-shows the page with an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing 'Select what you are importing', linked to the first radio (#notificationType), and the same message shown inline on the radio group (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:151-160; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 30; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:53-57)

The page ends with a single 'Continue' button: there is no 'Save and return to overview' button and no cancel link (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:48-53; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16)
The page's Back link goes to the all-types dashboard, and the service navigation highlights Dashboard (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10606-10608; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 15)
The page shows no Draft strip and no notification reference (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html:23-57; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 16 against action 44)

The origin page's Back link goes to the notification type question when the notification was started from it, to the live-animals dashboard when the notification was started from that dashboard's own create button, and to the notification overview when the origin page was opened from the overview (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10586-10600; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T3 action 10, T6 action 20; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:74,105; conflicts:c-011)

With Welsh chosen, every string on the notification type page (title, caption, heading, the four options, the error message and the Continue button) shows its Welsh counterpart (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)

sources.ref: T1 actions 15-44; T3 action 10; T6 action 20; TRACE C actions 8-16

rows.gate: Look at the cross-service start before anything builds on it: the type page in the INS front door, how Live animals hands over to the animals frontend's start (today a form post with its own request forgery token) and how the plants types hand over to the plants service, and the origin Back link's 'where the user came from' signal. The re-selection row, template creation's type question and the dashboard's 'Create new' button all copy this pattern.
rows.notes: Combines the type-page slices (question copy, options, validation, single Continue, Back link and navigation, no draft before a type) with the origin Back link (req-013), because the Back link to the type question can only be observed through the new start and both are reviewed on the same two pages. Merge order is frontend, insfrontend, tests: the animals frontend's start entry and Back-link signal must be live before the INS page sends users to them. The template branches of req-013 (Back to /templates/create while creating a template, and to the template review while editing one) are not written here because no real service has templates yet; they are carried by the templates area's requirements (req-1325 and the template-edit ones) and become observable with those rows. Per conflicts:c-006 the page keeps the 'Error: ' title prefix in its error state, as every real page does. The all-types dashboard's 'Create new' button itself (c-147) is the dashboard-home area's change; this row repoints whatever start control the dashboard has at the time to the type question. The Welsh criterion carries req-057's duty for the strings this row adds; req-057 itself sits in the origin row that finishes the page.

rows.title: Return to the type question from an existing live-animals notification
rows.detail: Once a live-animals notification exists, going back from its origin page to the notification type question shows Live animals already chosen. Keeping Live animals returns to the same notification. Choosing a different type clears every commodity and species chosen on that notification, so the type and commodity choices never disagree, and carries on to the start of the service that takes the new type. No non-live-animals type runs through the live-animals pages.
acceptanceCriteria: On a live-animals notification started from the type question, pressing Back on its origin page shows the 'What are you importing?' question with Live animals already selected (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10609; conflicts:c-007)

Pressing Continue with Live animals still chosen returns to that same notification's origin page, showing the same reference, and every commodity and species already chosen on it is kept (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11153-11155, 11163-11168)

Choosing a different type (for example Plants for planting) and pressing Continue lands on the start of the high-risk plants journey, and the live-animals notification, reopened from the dashboard, has no commodity or species chosen (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11153-11155; conflicts:c-007)
Starting afresh from the all-types dashboard still shows the question with nothing pre-selected (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10609; conflicts:c-007)
rows.notes: Depends on the row covering req-001 (the type question and the origin Back link to it must exist first); the combiner sets dependsOn. Kept apart from that row because it adds a cross-service write (clearing the live-animals notification's commodity and species answers when another type is chosen) that the first row does not need, and that row is already eleven criteria. Decision: c-007 limits re-selection to a notification that already exists and to the live-animals journey, so 'a different type' means one that hands over to the plants service; the live-animals notification is kept, with its commodities cleared, as the prototype does, rather than deleted. Frontend merges before insfrontend: the animals frontend must accept the existing notification's context and clear its commodities before the INS page relies on it.

rows.title: Start template creation from the notification type question
rows.detail: Creating a template starts from the same 'What are you importing?' question. In template mode its Back link returns to the templates list, and choosing a type stores it on a new Draft template and goes to the template name page instead of the origin page, so no notification is created.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting a new template from Manage templates shows the 'What are you importing?' question, whose Back link goes to Manage templates and whose service navigation highlights Templates (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:10606-10608; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T15 action 68)

Choosing a type and pressing Continue goes to the template name page ('Enter template name'), not the origin page, and no draft notification is created: the dashboard's notification list gains no new entry (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11157-11161; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-053; conflicts:c-007)
The template saved from that start holds the chosen type as a Draft (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11157-11161)
rows.notes: Observable only once the templates area's rows have built Manage templates, its 'Create new template' button (req-1293) and the template name page (req-1316), and once the row covering req-001 has built the type question; the combiner sets dependsOn on all of them. The templates area's req-1314 describes the same page in template mode (same options, no 'Template' caption yet, the usual error): combiner, merge this row into that one, since building them apart repeats the same page, set-up and review, and take that row's repos (template storage lives wherever the templates rows put it). The repos written here are only the type question's own.

rows.title: Country of origin becomes a search box
rows.detail: The country of origin control takes Design Release 2.1's copy and behaviour: no hint, a 'Search for a country' placeholder, a search icon instead of a drop-down arrow, results that appear only once the user types, matching anywhere in the name with the match in bold, and screen-reader announcements for the results and the choice. Within the accessibility duty (conflicts:c-006) it stays a labelled 'Country of origin' accessible type-ahead over a native select that still works without JavaScript.
acceptanceCriteria: The 'Country of origin' question shows no hint text, with or without JavaScript (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:49-103; conflicts:c-009)

With JavaScript, the empty country box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country'; without JavaScript the native select still begins with the blank 'Select a country' option (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:57-102; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T6 action 18; conflicts:c-009)
Focusing or clicking the empty country box opens no list; results appear only once the user types (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T7; conflicts:c-009)

The country box shows a search icon button at its right, with the visually hidden text 'Search', and no drop-down arrow (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:57-102; conflicts:c-009)

Typing lists every place whose name contains the typed letters anywhere, ignoring case (typing 'ance' lists France; typing 'NETH' lists Netherlands), with the matching letters shown in bold in each result (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T7 actions 15-19, T2 action 17; prototype:dr2-1-specs e2e/about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js:151-154; conflicts:c-009)

The results are labelled 'Country search results' for screen readers, a polite live region announces how many results are available, and choosing one announces 'Selected <country>', for example 'Selected France' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T7 action 19; prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:101; conflicts:c-009)

The control is still labelled 'Country of origin', choosing a country still saves it and shows it back when the page is reopened, and without JavaScript the native select still saves the chosen country (conflicts:c-006; repo:frontend origin.fit.spec.js 'native select submits and persists the country code')
With Welsh chosen, the placeholder, the 'Search' button text, the results label and the announcements show their Welsh counterparts (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)

sources.ref: T6 action 18; T7 actions 15-24; T2 actions 15-18

rows.notes: Combines the six country-control changes (hint, placeholder, no open-on-focus, search icon, contains-matching with bold, announcements): one control, one page, one review. The type-ahead component is shared with port of entry and transit countries (arrival-and-transit area), so the change is scoped to the country of origin instance unless the combiner finds those rows want the same behaviour, in which case the shared component change belongs to the foundation theme. The page changes visually, so this row's ladder refreshes the origin page's visual baseline too; req-058 (the final baseline) sits in the region code row that finishes the page.

rows.title: Region of origin code, internal reference hint and the finished origin page
rows.detail: The region of origin code question takes Design Release 2.1's hint, caps the box at 5 characters in the browser, and with JavaScript writes the country prefix live as the user picks a country, showing an empty prefix slot until then; without JavaScript the server-side prefix stays as DR1 shipped it. Answering No clears a saved code. The origin task is complete only when the country and the region question are answered and, under Yes, a code is held. The internal reference hint drops its 58-character sentence (the server still enforces the limit). Every new or changed string on the type and origin pages has Welsh, and the origin page's stored visual baseline is updated to the finished page.
acceptanceCriteria: The region of origin code question's hint reads 'Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:133-135; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-010)

The region code box stops typing at 5 characters and has autocomplete and spellcheck turned off; a longer code still gets the server's existing error (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/partials/region-of-origin-code-input.html:19-29; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-010)

With JavaScript, picking France in the country box makes the region code prefix 'FR', and then picking Netherlands makes it 'NL', with no form submission (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T5 actions 40-53, T7 action 24; conflicts:c-008)
Before any country is chosen, the revealed region code box shows an empty prefix in front of it, which fills in once a country is picked (trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-008)
Without JavaScript, the prefix still shows the saved or submitted country's code once the page is re-shown, as today (conflicts:c-008; trace:animals-fit origin-f-348e9 call@3019)

Changing a saved Yes answer with code FR-75 to No and saving clears the code: the review page shows 'Not applicable' for the region of origin code, and choosing Yes again shows an empty code box (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:11196-11201; trace:prototype-dr2-1 TRACE H action 165; conflicts:c-010)

The overview's 'Where is this consignment coming from?' task reads 'Complete' only when a country is chosen and the region of origin code question is answered: a country saved with the region question unanswered does not read 'Complete', a country with No reads 'Complete', and a country with Yes and a code reads 'Complete' (prototype:dr2-1-source app/routes.js:402-415; trace:animals-fit origin-c-706f0, origin-f-750ee call@3749)

The internal reference hint reads 'Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.', with no 'It can be up to 58 characters.' sentence; a reference over 58 characters still gets the server's error naming the limit (prototype:dr2-1-source app/views/design-release-2.1/origin-of-the-import.html:155-169; trace:prototype-dr2-1 T1 action 44; conflicts:c-011)

With Welsh chosen, every new or changed string on the type and origin pages (the type page copy, the country placeholder and search texts, the region hint and the internal reference hint) shows its Welsh counterpart, and no removed hint (the country hint, the 58-character sentence) is left in the Welsh copy (repo:frontend features/origin/copy/copy.cy.js:1-3)

The end-to-end suite's full-page visual baseline of the origin page shows the changed page (no country hint, the search box with its placeholder and icon, the new region hint and the shorter internal reference hint), and the visual check passes against it (trace:e2e T16 expect@50, screencast page@da77b720)

rows.notes: Combines the region code slices (hint, maxlength, live prefix, empty prefix slot, No clears the code), the origin task's completeness rule, the internal reference hint, the Welsh sweep and the visual baseline: all change the same origin page and its one baseline, so building them apart repeats the page, ladder and baseline refresh. Depends on the country search box row (req-015 to req-020): the live prefix follows the country picked in that control (DR1 inc-079 tied the live prefix to the country control), and the baseline must show the finished page. The combiner sets dependsOn. Completeness: Yes without a code cannot be saved through the page (the page holds the trader with 'Enter the region of origin code'), so the 'Yes needs a code' half of req-034 is guarded by the page's existing validation and the criterion observes the reachable cases; the builder still adds the rule to the origin obligation so a stored Yes with no code is never Complete. req-057's Welsh duty is also written into the type-question and country rows for the strings they add; it is listed here, where the last strings land.
